issues.title: Handler logic mixed in schema file
issues.description: The rule requires that schema and handler logic are separated into different files. However, the schema file `booking.output.ts` now contains a handler method `cleanEmailForDisplay()` that performs email validation and transformation logic, mixing schema definition with handler logic in the same file.
issues.rule_name: Schema and Handler Files Must Be Separated with Type-Safe Patterns

issues.title: Lost `this` context in displayGuests mapping causes runtime error
issues.description: In the `getOutputBooking` method at line 171, the code passes `this.getDisplayEmail` directly to the `map` function without binding the `this` context. This causes a runtime error because when `getDisplayEmail` is invoked inside the `map` callback, `this` will be `undefined`, resulting in "Cannot read property 'replace' of undefined" or similar errors. The arrow function `(guest: string) => this.getDisplayEmail(guest)` was removed, which was necessary to preserve the `this` binding. This will break all bookings that have guests.

issues.title: Recurring seated bookings returned in wrong order
issues.description: In the `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings` method at line 424, the sort operation that orders bookings chronologically by start time has been removed. The original code sorted bookings with `.sort((a, b) => new Date(a.start).getTime() - new Date(b.start).getTime())` to ensure they are returned in chronological order. Without this sorting, recurring bookings will be returned in an arbitrary order (based on how they were stored in the database or map), which breaks the expected API contract and will confuse clients expecting chronological ordering of recurring events.

issues.title: Unnecessary regex processing on literal "unknown" string
issues.description: In the `getHost` method at line 219, when the user is null/unknown, the code now calls `this.getDisplayEmail("unknown")` instead of directly setting `displayEmail: "unknown"`. This causes unnecessary regex processing on the literal string "unknown" which has no CUID suffix to remove. While this doesn't break functionality, it adds unnecessary computational overhead and is semantically incorrect - the getDisplayEmail method is designed to strip CUID suffixes from actual email addresses, not process placeholder strings. This represents a performance issue and code smell that violates the principle of only processing data when necessary.

issues.title: Service file uses disallowed '.service.ts' suffix / naming convention violation
issues.description: Rule 1 disallows dot-suffix service filenames like '.service.ts' and requires service files to be named '<Entity>Service.ts' with matching PascalCase. This PR modifies a service located at 'services/output.service.ts', which violates the naming convention.
issues.rule_name: Rule 1: Repository and Service Classes Must Follow Naming Conventions

issues.title: Line(s) exceed the 110 character line width requirement
issues.description: The added assignment line is longer than the 110 character limit required by the Biome formatting rules for TS/JS files.
issues.rule_name: Rule 3: Use Biome for Code Formatting with Standardized Configuration

issues.description: The PR introduces improperly indented JSON (the 'required' key is moved to column 1). This indicates the JSON was not kept formatted per the repository’s formatting/lint-staged expectations (Biome format for JSON).

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25593 - fix(api): return original email without OAuth suffix in bookings

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds a `displayEmail` field next to the existing `email` field across API v2 (2024-08-13) booking outputs. The new value strips a `+{cuid}` suffix using the regex `/\+[a-zA-Z0-9]{25}/`, so `email` keeps the OAuth-suffixed value for backwards compatibility. It covers hosts, attendees, `bookingFieldsResponses` (`email` and `displayGuests`), and `reassignedTo`. The OpenAPI JSON, the DTO classes, and a broad set of e2e tests are updated to match.

The additive approach is sound and avoids a breaking change to `email`. However, I found three real problems. First, the unanchored regex strips any 25-character alphanumeric run after a `+`, so ordinary plus-addressed emails get mangled. Second, the diff silently removes the sort in `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings`, which is unrelated to the feature. Third, several new test assertions compare the response to itself and cannot meaningfully fail.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The regex can corrupt the `displayEmail` for ordinary plus-addressed emails, which is the field this PR exists to get right. It is a one-line fix, but it should land before merge. The silent sort removal is an unrelated behavior change that should be reverted or justified. The test and documentation issues are smaller but affect confidence in the change.

architecture.overview:
API v2 booking responses are built in `OutputBookingsService_2024_08_13` (`output.service.ts`). It takes a database booking, maps `user`, `attendees`, and `bookingFieldsResponses` into the response shape, and returns it. The DTOs in `packages/platform/types/bookings/2024-08-13/outputs/booking.output.ts` define the Swagger/OpenAPI shape. Managed users have their email stored with a `+{cuid}` suffix so that users from different OAuth clients don't collide.

This PR does not change storage or the write path. It adds a read-time transformation: a private `getDisplayEmail` helper strips the suffix and attaches the result as a new `displayEmail` key on hosts, attendees, reassignedTo, and bookingFieldsResponses (plus `displayGuests`). The original `email` values are passed through unchanged, which keeps existing clients working. The OpenAPI JSON is hand-edited to advertise the new properties.
steps: Entry point: `bookings.service.ts` calls the output service for every booking response (single, list, recurring, seated, reassigned).
`OutputBookingsService_2024_08_13.getOutputBooking` and its siblings map the DB booking into the response; this is where `hosts` (via `getHost`), `attendees`, and `bookingFieldsResponses` are built.
The PR adds `getDisplayEmail` (`output.service.ts` line ~96) and calls it for each email field, so `email` stays raw and `displayEmail` is the cleaned copy.
The PR also adds `displayEmail` / `displayGuests` to the DTO classes and the OpenAPI JSON so the docs and Swagger describe the new fields.
Watch the regex (it decides what gets stripped) and the unrelated change to `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings`, which drops its sort.

findings.title: Regex strips real characters from plus-addressed emails
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/output.service.ts`, `getDisplayEmail` (around lines 96-98) uses the unanchored regex `/\+[a-zA-Z0-9]{25}/`. That regex corrupts ordinary plus-addressed emails such as `john+<26 chars>@x.com`, which becomes `johnz@x.com`. Tighten it so it only removes a CUID-shaped suffix directly before `@` (for example `\+c[a-z0-9]{24}(?=@)`). Keep the function pure and reuse it everywhere it's already called. Check that the pattern matches the one in `google-calendar.service.ts`, and add unit tests for a plus-tagged email that must be preserved.

findings.title: Unrelated sort removed from getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/output.service.ts`, `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings` (around line 424) was changed from `return transformed.sort((a, b) => new Date(a.start).getTime() - new Date(b.start).getTime());` to `return transformed;`. That sort is unrelated to the displayEmail feature and changes response ordering. Restore the original sort line so behavior matches the sibling methods, or move the removal into a separate PR with justification.

findings.title: Seated-attendee tests compare the response to itself
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/controllers/e2e/seated-bookings.e2e-spec.ts`, the `displayEmail` expectations near lines 280 and 421 compare against `createdSeatedBooking.attendees[0].displayEmail` and `attendee?.displayEmail`, which come from the same server output being tested. Replace them with the known input email with the `+cuid` suffix stripped, the same way `managed-user-bookings.e2e-spec.ts` does. Assert against values that are fixed by the test setup, not against other response fields.

findings.title: CI breaking-change check suppressed for new response fields
findings.fixPrompt: In `.github/oasdiff-err-ignore.txt`, the six new lines (around lines 5-8) suppress oasdiff errors for booking endpoints. Confirm each entry matches an actual, intended schema change, and add a short comment above the block explaining that these are the intentional `displayEmail` additions. Remove any entry that covers an unrelated change.

findings.title: Output helper logic duplicated three times and DTO helper is dead code
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/output.service.ts`, the `displayEmail` and `displayGuests` assignment block is duplicated in several `getOutput*` methods. Extract it into one private helper, such as `attachDisplayFields(booking)`, and call it from each place. Use an arrow or explicit lambda for `.map` so the call doesn't depend on an unbound `this`. Also remove the unused static `cleanEmailForDisplay` in `packages/platform/types/bookings/2024-08-13/outputs/booking.output.ts` (around lines 60-62), since nothing calls it.

findings.title: Hand-edited OpenAPI JSON has broken indentation
findings.body:
In `docs/api-reference/v2/openapi.json`, the `"required"` arrays that gained `displayEmail` lost their indentation. Each line starts at column 0 instead of matching the surrounding keys. The JSON stays valid, but it's clearly hand-edited and will fail any formatter check. The PR says the spec was auto-generated, so regenerating it would produce the correct formatting.

::diff{file="docs/api-reference/v2/openapi.json" lines="31726-31736"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `docs/api-reference/v2/openapi.json`, the `"required": [` lines added for `displayEmail` (around lines 31726-31736 and the matching spots in the attendee, seated attendee, and reassigned schemas) are not indented like their neighbors. Re-run the OpenAPI generator or the repo's formatter so the file matches the project style, and confirm the JSON still parses.

findings.title: displayEmail added consistently across output types with backwards-compatible email
findings.body: The PR keeps every original `email` field unchanged and adds `displayEmail` next to it. Existing clients don't break, and clients that want the clean address can use the new field. The e2e tests cover the host, attendee, guest, and reassigned cases, and the `unknown` fallback for a missing user is handled.
